extracts.title: Extract Two
extracts.context: You hear two friends discussing the practice of urban foraging, which is picking nuts and fruit from around a city.

questions.text: Why does the woman think urban foraging is popular?

options.text: People seek a strong connection with nature.
Wild food is guaranteed to be organic.
It can save money on grocery bills.

questions.text: How do they both feel about urban foraging becoming possible in their local park?

options.text: worried that many plants will be destroyed
hopeful that plant identification courses will be held
surprised that local residents weren't consulted about it

parts.passageContent:
Larry explains that butterflies are less effective than bees at pollinating plants.

Larry has done research into plants that have a strong _____(30)_____ and how they attract butterflies.

Larry points out that butterflies are a vital link in the food _____(31)_____, both as a prey and predators.

Butterflies can be a good form of _____(32)_____ control, which means they can be a benefit to farmers.

Butterflies are known by scientists to be good indicators of climate change.

A type of butterfly called the Checkerspot now populates areas at higher _____(33)_____ than in the past.

Butterflies can attract _____(34)_____ to an area and boost the local economy.

The European Meadow Brown butterfly produces a natural _____(35)_____ which may be of use to humans.
